editorial.headline: Painting: Open Nationally, Viable for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers finishing-stage interior and exterior painting for buildings and civil works, with full foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Painting is the finishing work that gives buildings and civil structures their final surface. Under code 43303, the activity covers interior and exterior painting undertaken in completing residential buildings, non-residential buildings, and civil works. Its scope is practical and defined: it concerns painting those structures as part of their completion. Roof painting is expressly outside the activity, creating a clear boundary around what the registration represents.

The activity is open at every business scale stated in the record: Micro, Small, Medium, and Large. That breadth gives the code a straightforward operational identity. It is a registration for painting work across interior and exterior building surfaces and civil structures, rather than a narrower description confined to one property type or one side of a building. For a founder, the useful starting point is therefore the work itself: finishing-stage painting, with roof work excluded.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is just as direct. The activity is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record does not impose a national foreign-ownership cap below full ownership for this activity. The national picture is not conditional or partial: this is an activity that can be registered with foreign investment up to full foreign ownership, across the listed business scales.

Bali requires its own reading, because the province permanently blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record identifies its OSS risk at the Large scale as Medium-High/High, which places it outside the moratorium block. The honest conclusion is therefore clear: a foreign investor can register this painting activity in Bali today. Its Bali status is not a warning that the activity is closed; it reflects that the activity sits at an eligible higher-risk position rather than within the permanently blocked risk bands.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this painting activity in Bali today because it sits outside the province’s PMA moratorium block.
